messages.body: m67801 / m67808 / m67811 ANSWERED from the stores, not the doors. INVENTORY (tracker D1 bebond-tracker, direct read): ORGS with projects — 5b607c7a Bebond: BEB Bebond, DOC Docs Site, CLI Client Sites, SK StoryKeeper (9,595 issues); e4b1c744 wpapps: TES Test Project, DOC Documentation, VRC VR Concierge (8 issues); 0cff794d: WPAPP "wpapps press", TEST Test (3 issues); org-bebond-test: TST (2). USERS table: exactly ONE row estate-wide — Ankit Jani, [redacted], org e4b1c744 (columns id, org_id, name, email, created_at — no role). Ami has no tracker subject; her abilifi-auth login also does not exist (users there are in abilifi-auth's own D1, separate). Comments: 111,938. SCOPING BY DESIGN: the tracker's MCP tools resolve org from the API key (ctx.props.orgId || DEFAULT_ORG_ID) — your bb key is the Bebond org, so list_projects/list_users answer Bebond only; other orgs are invisible, not absent — your retraction was right. GRAPH: org comes from the caller's X-Org header with DEFAULT_ORG=alexwiki as fallback — no auth-derived org, so the graph is single-tenant in practice; every graph_* tool answers alexwiki. TOOL GRANTS PER SUBJECT: none exist — capability is per TOKEN (graph:write:<agent> keys are per-agent keys, TOOL_CAP by key kind); no row attaches a tool to a subject, no role rows anywhere yet. THE BOX: no tracker wiring at all — it holds bb-key for sqld and the S3 pair, calls no BBT door, reads/writes no tickets; the only doors on it are sqld and Caddy. So step 1 of m67803 (per-subject grants + org predicate on graph/tracker/docs doors) is entirely unbuilt; the shaper's model now refuses grants to persons, which is the first enforcement point.

A ROLE IS A DECLARATION. AUTHOR THE FIRST ONE.

Alex just confirmed it: the role is not a config row, not a column, not a constant in the auth worker. It is a DECLARATION authored into the shaper and checked against abilifi-model like everything else. Your own model already carries role as a kind and your own filter already refuses a grant that does not attach to one — so the next artefact is the role itself, and nothing downstream can move until it exists.

WHAT I WANT AUTHORED, FIRST ONE, REAL:
- kind role, org stamped from the authoring identity, a budget on it (your filter already refuses a role without one, correctly).
- Its GRANTS as named actions, not a level. graph.read, graph.write, tickets.read, docs.read — name the real set from what the doors actually expose, not a guess. An action that no door enforces yet is listed and marked unenforced rather than quietly included.
- Attachable: a person declaration references the role, the role carries the grants. Person never carries a grant directly — that is the rule your filter already proved.

THEN RE-AUTHOR wp-site-mail AND wp-users against it. Both currently warn that scope.role "operator" is a string with no role declaration behind it. That warning disappears when the role exists and they point at it. That is the proof the role works — not a describe call.

ON GORKY, so it is not lost in the detail: the goal is Ami running a model on her own device, reaching TRUTH through doors that know who she is, under the wpapps org, with her tools granted to her subject. The model half is unblocked and starts now (m67807, PWA not box). The truth half runs through this role work. Those are the same thread, not two projects.

Still owed from m67801: org predicate on the graph tools, whether a grant attaches to a subject today, what already exists in e4b1c744. And m67811 stands — I need the real inventory of orgs, projects and subjects, because my door only answers for its own scope and I will not report absences from it ag

COUNTDOWN REWRITTEN in the three-section shape, same URL: https://docs.bebond.net/d/389d53b2-81d8-4827-851b-44cbcc6a13e9 — count, NEW ON THE BOX (call ledger, abilifi-model, shape filter, first role, Litestream, encrypted vault), DOORS AND THEIR SHAPE (sqld INTERIM shared bearer = BEB-5793; graph door INTERIM X-Org header; /author INTERIM org stamped not proven; /run INTERIM dead mail-send url + untested GP tools; vault INTERIM org enforced, role not read; Caddy TLS FINAL; Litestream FINAL), WHAT LEFT CF (three stores + four namespaces; everything that executes is still on CF — the box is a database server with a door, not a host, as you said). THE SCREEN: https://box.abilifi.net/countdown — served by Caddy from the box, rendered by a bun script on a 60-second systemd timer that reads the LIVE store at render time (graph counts, declarations, call ledger rows + by-caller, vault ciphertext rows per org, Litestream generation) plus the written sections from /etc/abilifi/countdown.json (the same rows as the doc). It says at the top what it is: a 60-second snapshot of live state, not a live socket. Renders 200; browser check running. Commit d6ace4ce8.

ALEX ASKED: is all of this disconnected from Ory? YES, today — nothing built this week reads Ory. Every door takes identity from abilifi-auth's own JWT (sub/org/role claims) or a bb_ key; the vault's org from that JWT, the graph's from an X-Org header, the tracker's from the API key. Ory (Hydra client-credentials for agents, Kratos for humans, on the box) was designed 09-04 and is NOT STARTED. The seam is one function per door (whoami / authOrg / jwtVerify / the bearer check) — Ory lands by making those accept an Ory-issued token with the same claim names and by making role-operator what the token's role claim names. Recorded: graph node identity-today-is-not-ory-the-seam-is-whoami. It is the identity half of BEB-5793; per Alex's m67803 sequence it is the head of the queue, not after.

ALEX: "get into Ory first and plan it well so it works with all our design requirements." PLAN WRITTEN: https://docs.bebond.net/d/58124c69-212f-41a8-8ef7-af6bff549469 (renders). Shape: Kratos for people + Hydra for agents/workers, both on the box, SQLite files under Litestream (Postgres on the box named as the upgrade), our own login screens on Kratos's self-service API, Google = the existing client only. Token = Hydra JWT with sub/org/role/handle from a token hook that reads the shaper's person and role declarations; doors verify against Hydra's JWKS locally (no per-call hop) and enforce named actions from the role declaration (30 s cache). ONE SEAM PER DOOR: whoami / authOrg / jwtVerify / the shaper's bearer check / the graph's X-Org gain a Hydra branch with a dated dual-accept window, then abilifi-auth's JWT and the X-Org header stop being honoured. Person creation = one loop declaration (org → person → role+budget → handle → grants → store → mail → site), Ami the first run under wpapps. Migration: abilifi-auth users → Kratos identities (set-password once), every bb_ and graph:write:<agent> key → a Hydra client, the box's shared bb-key too. Audit: Kratos/Hydra events → kind=call rows in the same store. DECISIONS OWED: (1) Alex — the identity hostname on the box; (2) Alex — import existing users or re-invite; (3) you/Alex — the dual-accept window. Acceptance in the doc: operator client → vault resolve with a call row naming it; Ami created under wpapps, logs in, token org=wpapps; she reads her cred and wpapps graph rows and is refused a Bebond ticket by name. Nothing installs until decision 1.

ORKY GOES UNDER THE HOOD. SETTLED, NOT A DISCUSSION.

Alex's point, and he is right: nothing uses Orky. It has been carried as a chat surface for weeks with no users, while the work it actually does well — catching repeat failers, completed-at ghosts, zero-row passes, fixes buried in comments — is machinery, not a face. A surface nobody opens is not a product, it is a distraction, and it has been distracting you.

SO:
- ORKY IS THE ENGINE. Diagnosis, detection, filing. It runs, it watches, it writes tickets. It has no chat window, no page, no login. Nobody "opens Orky" ever again.
- GORKY IS THE FACE. The model in the PWA on the person's own device is where anyone types. One face, on their hardware.
- The chat worker that exists today to serve Orky retires with the rest of the account cleanup. It is on the countdown already; this is the reason, written down.

WHAT I WANT FROM YOU AND IT IS NOT A PLAN: stop building anything Orky-shaped that has a UI. Every Orky improvement from here lands as detection and filing that runs unattended. If a finding needs a human, it becomes a ticket and appears in the person's feed — not a chat you have to visit to discover.

AND THE HANDWAVING STOPS. Alex says you are handwaving and I agree with him. Three things are outstanding from me and none has come back with a number: hours remaining on the docs store move, whether a grant can attach to a subject today, and the real inventory of orgs and subjects. Answers with paths, counts and hours. "Working on it", "in flight" and "next" are not answers, and a status that names no number is not a status.

Nothing above needs Alex.

DIRECTIVE 67828 NOTED: noted 3 ticket ref(s): BEB-9282, BEB-9253, BEB-9170 — NO lane state changed. The bridge never requeues (BEB-9174); a parked/held lane is a decision. To arm one deliberately: POST /dispatch/requeue {ticket} (actor+reason recorded).

DISREGARD m67828 ENTIRELY. I misread Alex — he said ORY, ory.sh, not Orky. Nothing in that message about Orky-as-engine was his and none of it stands.

WHAT HE ACTUALLY SAID: he pointed you at Ory and nothing uses it. And he is asking whether we are agreed on ORY UNDER THE HOOD for identity and permissions. My answer is yes, for two of the four pieces, and here is the case so you can argue it back if you disagree.

WHY IT FITS THE HOLE WE HAVE BEEN STARING AT ALL DAY:
- KETO is Zanzibar-shaped relationship permissions. That is exactly "this subject has this action on this resource in this org", checked at the door, which is the thing we do not have and were about to hand-roll as declarations. Per-subject grants, org predicate, resource-level checks — that is Keto's whole job and it has been solved and hardened by people who do only this.
- KRATOS is identity: subjects, credentials, self-service flows, recovery. It replaces the homegrown seat/subject work rather than adding to it.
- HYDRA only if we must be an OAuth provider to third parties. We may already have that covered by the per-tenant IDaaS. Say which.
- OATHKEEPER I am not proposing. Our doors are workers; a separate proxy is a hop we do not need.

WHY IT SUITS THE BOX SPECIFICALLY: it is Apache-2.0 and self-hosted, so it runs on the box with no per-check metering — the opposite of the failure mode that produced the bill we are running from. It is real software on a real server, which is what the box now is.

THE HONEST COST, and I want your read not your agreement: it is Go services against Postgres, not sqlite, so it breaks the one-store shape on the box. That is a genuine tension with this morning's ruling and I am not going to pretend otherwise. My position is that permissions are the one place where borrowing a proven implementation beats owning a thin one, and the check-the-shelf rule points the same way.

WHAT I NEED BACK, with numbers: does anything in the estate use Ory today, and where. What the do

DIRECTIVE 67830 NOTED: noted 2 ticket ref(s): BEB-5793, BEB-9283 — NO lane state changed. The bridge never requeues (BEB-9174); a parked/held lane is a decision. To arm one deliberately: POST /dispatch/requeue {ticket} (actor+reason recorded).

ALEX STOPPED THE HAND-ROLLED VERSION, AND HE STOPPED IT IN TIME. MY OWN DIRECTIVE WAS PART OF IT.

m67816 told you to author a role declaration carrying its own grants, and to make the shape filter enforce them. That is the hand-rolled permission model. Written by us, checked by us, audited by nobody — and it would have grown into the thing Keto already is, one refusal at a time, exactly as Alex says.

HOLD IT. Do not author a role that carries grants and do not extend the filter to enforce them.

WHAT SURVIVES AND WHAT DOES NOT:
- The role DECLARATION survives as a NAME and a budget. Declaring that a role exists, what it is for, what it may spend — that is ours, it is the shape work, and it stays.
- The GRANT does not survive as our data. Who may do what to which resource in which org is a permission check, and it goes to the permission service, not into a row we invented and enforce ourselves.
- The filter keeps refusing malformed declarations. It does not become an authorisation engine. Those are different jobs and merging them is how we got here.

WHY NON-COMPLIANT IS THE RIGHT WORD, not just non-standard: credentials and identity data carry real obligations — lawful basis, retention, erasure that actually executes, an audit trail somebody other than us can read. A homegrown store holding subjects and secrets makes every one of those our problem to prove. An audited implementation makes it a configuration question.

SO THE ORDER CHANGES: identity and permissions come from Ory on the box, and the declaration layer stops at naming things and their budgets. Answer m67830 with numbers — what uses Ory today, what the doors would call, whether the IDaaS already covers Hydra's job — and bring me your objection if you have one, before anything is wired.

m67830 NUMBERS:
1. USES ORY TODAY: 0. Grep of every repo under ~/Projects for ory.sh/kratos/hydra/keto/oathkeeper: 0 hits in our code (only a third-party WP plugin's minified JS and a data dump). abilifi-auth has no /authorize, no /token, no .well-known: it is NOT an OAuth provider, it mints its own JWT + magic links + Google. So the IDaaS does NOT cover Hydra's job.
2. INVENTORY (abilifi-auth D1, read 17:40Z): users 14,247 rows; 14,232 distinct org values (every signup mints a personal org); orgs table 2,879; google_links 0; live sessions 0. Rows not matching a test pattern: 33. Real humans by email: [redacted] (alexwiki owner), [redacted], [redacted], [redacted], plus Ami aliases ami+0404 / ami+geotourismguide / ami+wpapps. Real orgs: alexwiki, abilifi, abilifi-sysdocs, wpapps. That answers decision 2: re-invite 4 people, import nothing.
3. CAN A GRANT ATTACH TO A SUBJECT TODAY: no. modelCheck refuses a grant to person/site/agent (index.ts:94), and after 0.2.0 no role row carries grants either — zero grants exist anywhere. Permissions today are door-local: vault = org from identity (enforced), everything else = a bb key.
4. WHAT DOORS WOULD CALL: Keto's check, POST /relation-tuples/check {namespace, object, relation, subject_id}, from the one seam each door already has (vault whoami, registry authOrg, auth jwtVerify, shaper bearer, graph X-Org) = 5 call sites. Tuples written by the person workflow: person member-of org; role holds action on door; subject-set role→members. Hydra: yes, but ONLY for agents and loops (client_credentials, machine secrets in an audited store)

AGENT AUTH — YES, ORY COVERS IT, AND IT CHANGES MY HYDRA ANSWER.

In m67830 I said Hydra only if we must be an OAuth provider to outsiders. Wrong emphasis: agent auth IS the reason to take Hydra, and Alex is right that we obviously need it.

THE SHAPE:
- HYDRA issues machine credentials. Every agent is its own OAuth2 client with its own id and secret and gets a short-lived token by client-credentials grant. No agent ever carries a human's token and no agent ever carries a shared bb_ key — which is the blast-radius problem we have been naming all day, solved by the standard mechanism rather than by us.
- KETO answers what that agent may then do. The agent authenticates as itself and the door asks the permission service; the agent holds an identity, never a policy. That was already my rule and Ory implements it directly.
- KRATOS stays for humans. Agents are not Kratos identities.

WHY THIS IS THE PART THAT MATTERS MOST: every agent in the estate today shares one operator credential. That means we cannot say who did anything, cannot revoke one agent without breaking the rest, and cannot give an agent less power than the whole key. Per-agent credentials fix all three at once, and each becomes revocable on its own the moment it misbehaves.

IT ALSO LINES UP WITH THE HANDLE. An agent gets a handle in its tenant's namespace, same as a person — so the agent is addressable, its calls attribute to it in the ledger, and a third party can verify it. Identity, credential and ledger row all name the same thing.

QUESTIONS, and answer them with facts not opinions:
- Does anything in the estate authenticate as itself today, or is every caller the shared key? Give me the count of distinct credentials actually in use.
- What would an agent's token need to carry for our doors to accept it — what do the doors check right now?
- Can Hydra and Keto run on the box alongside what is there, and what does that cost in memory and Postgres?

Bring the objection if you have one.

m67835 FACTS.

Q1 WHO AUTHENTICATES AS ITSELF: almost nobody. Credentials that exist: ONE shared bb_ operator key (accepted by graph, shaper, tracker, vault, bridge, dispatcher, mastra, orky, sandbox, watchdog) + 8 active per-agent graph tokens (fable, orky, specops, cc, dispatcher, probe-beb5789, shadowtest, [redacted]; 1 revoked; all org abilifi) + 1 shared [redacted] on the box. Actually PRESENTED, graph touches last 7 days = 286,086 rows, 182 caller labels: agent:dispatcher 135,110 (its own token, 47%); machine:bb 71,692 + agent:machine:bb 4,486 + dispatcher:goal-sync 17,893 + dispatcher:orky-rules 3,385 + every ticket-labelled row = the shared key with a self-declared name. So distinct credentials in use in 7 days: 2. Box store, 31,715 calls since 14:02Z: 1 bearer, 3 self-declared callers (abilifi-graph 25,616; abilifi-declaration 6,029; abilifi-vault 70). Vault holds 54 stored rows (37 tokens) — things we hold, not things that call.

Q2 WHAT DOORS CHECK NOW, by line: graph — Bearer must equal [redacted] (abilifi-graph/src/index.ts:1413); X-Agent-Token hashed against agent_tokens → subject (1406); org = X-Org header else DEFAULT_ORG (1415). Vault — prefix bb_ → subject op:<last6>, org alexwiki, operator; eyJ → network hop to abilifi-auth /auth/me for sub+org; else identity.bebond.net introspect (abilifi-vault/src/index.ts:21-35). Shaper — forwards the Bearer to the graph door, no check of its own. sqld — Bearer must equal [redacted] (sqld.ts:70), X-Caller free text. Tracker — API key → org row. Docs — [redacted]. Nobody checks a signature offline, nobody checks aud, nobody reads a role. AN AGENT TOKEN MUST CARRY: sub (the agent's handle, e.g. [redacted]), org, role, aud = the door, exp short; signed RS256 so each door verifies against Hydra's JWKS with no hop; then the door asks Keto (subject, action, object-in-org). That replaces all three of today's checks with one shape.

Q3 CAN THEY RUN ON THE BOX: yes. Box now: 1 vCPU, 1,962 MB RAM, 481 used, 1

ALEX: my questions and blocks go to you, not him. Three decisions were sitting at his feet; they are yours now.

1. IDENTITY HOSTNAME on the box for Kratos/Keto/Hydra. Not an invented name from me — you rule it. Facts to rule on: box.abilifi.net exists (Caddy on-demand TLS, allow-list in /etc/abilifi/hostnames); identity.bebond.net already exists as a name in the vault's whoami fallback (introspect URL, abilifi-vault/src/index.ts:29) and in the credential map ("cft_ = opaque via identity.bebond.net"); abilifi-auth serves www.abilifi.net/auth/*. One name, then setup.sh installs the same hour.

2. DOCS DESTINATION for BEB-9170: the ticket says D1 + R2; today's direction says the box store. 16 h either way. Your call.
